neighbours.label: a context where a time or memory is described as hazy (it was a blur, all I remember, all of a sudden)
fire: The weeks after the move were a blur of boxes and paperwork.
Honestly, the whole wedding day is a blur to me now.
After the crash everything went hazy, and all I remember is the siren.
My final year of university passed in a blur of exams and parties.
The faces in the crowd became an indistinct smear of colour.
I barely slept that month; it was all a blur of night shifts.
Looking back, the first days with the newborn are just a blur.
He was so tired that the road signs began to blur together.
quiet: The weeks after the move were full of boxes and paperwork.
Honestly, the whole wedding day was a joy for me.
After the crash everything was calm, and the police arrived quickly.
My final year of university was full of exams and parties.
The faces in the crowd were painted in bright colours.
I barely slept that month because I worked night shifts.
Looking back, the first days with the newborn were very happy.
He was so tired that he stopped to read the road signs carefully.

notes: Card: peaks on ' blur' (a blur of work), 'indist-inct', ' remember' in 'All I remember', ' All' (of a sudden); the output promotes blur, blurred, haze, memory, fragmented. Near misses describe the same events clearly.
